idea: Repair is a transmission problem: the scarce thing is not parts or technique but the accompanied decade of wrong guesses that makes diagnosis possible.

sources.cite: J. Parker, The repair shop stays open

units.text: The shop is found by breakage and word of mouth, never by advertising.

span.quote: He never advertised. People found him because something had broken and someone told them where to go.

units.text: The shelf of dead-stock parts is a promise to the owner with no other option, not inventory.

span.quote: He said the shelf was not inventory. It was a promise to whoever walked in with a twenty-year-old saw and no other option.
I used to think this was sentiment.

units.text: The shelf is arithmetic done on a longer horizon than the books track.

span.quote: It is arithmetic done on a longer horizon than a quarter.

units.text: Repair is mostly diagnosis — listening, not wrenching.

span.quote: What the trade calls a repair is mostly diagnosis. Two hours of listening, ten minutes of wrench.

units.text: The head tilt at a running engine tells you the shape of the afternoon.

span.quote: He would start an engine and stand there with his head tilted, and the tilt told you whether the afternoon was going to be simple.

units.text: Hearing an engine takes ten years and a great many wrong guesses.

span.quote: He said it took ten years and a great many wrong guesses.

units.text: Naming the failure: broken in a way that is cheap to fix and expensive to explain.

span.quote: A machine arrives broken in a way that is cheap to fix and expensive to explain.

units.text: Both repairs run; only the honest one teaches the owner about the thing he owns.

span.quote: Both machines run when they leave. Only one owner learns anything about the thing he owns.

units.text: The drift toward unrepairability reads as somebody's plot.

span.quote: None of this is a conspiracy.

units.text: Unrepairability is what happens when the assembler never meets the person who opens the product a second time.

span.quote: It is what happens when the person who assembles a product never meets the person who opens it a second time.

units.text: The shop closed for transmission reasons, not demand: nobody stood at the bench for the necessary decade.

span.quote: Not because the work dried up. Because the work required my uncle, and my uncle turned seventy-four, and nobody had stood beside him at the bench for the ten years it takes to hear an engine.

units.text: The loss worth counting is the bench — the accompanied decade of wrong guesses — not the shop.

span.quote: Not the shop. The bench, and the decade of wrong guesses that only happens next to someone who has already made them.

tensions.note: if the longer-horizon arithmetic pays, the decade at the bench should have been worth funding — the closure says nobody priced it, and the essay never names what the books still do not track

gaps.label: the lever — what would make the assembler meet the opener
whether the decade compresses — the apprenticeship floor is asserted, not argued
